- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model should not overreact — cap forecast slope to avoid overshoot; reduce rate of increase by 10–20%.
- If official event net is bearish (supply net <0) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model should not ignore downward pressure — reduce forecast mean by 2–5% relative to prior period.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed or negative — if forecast is trending sharply, apply a 1–2 day lag correction to align with recent price behavior.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model should not over-forecast upside — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak observed in prior 7–14 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., -0.50 or -1.00), model should not assume continuation — apply downward bias correction of 1–3% per bearish sentiment event.
